nv_rad_cliff_the.blurb: A band of sandstone on the lower flank of Whiskey Peak in Black Velvet Canyon, Red Rock, reached by the standard trail toward Frogland and then across the descent gully. All 15 routes are trad, mostly single-pitch with the odd two-pitch line, and nearly all fall between 5.6 and 5.9, with one or two lines at 5.10 and above. It suits climbers building trad experience on short, moderate cracks. The cliff drops into shade in the afternoon, which makes it a pleasant place to finish a day or to warm up before heading higher on Whiskey Peak. Descents are generally rappels with two ropes.

nv_refrigerator_wall.blurb: A wall stretching along the south side of the main fork of Icebox Canyon in Red Rock, a short stroll west from the canyon trailhead. Nearly all of its 15 routes are trad, plus a single sport line, on varnished sandstone. Most climbs sit in the 5.10 range, with a good handful at 5.11, a couple at 5.9 and one 5.12. Lines vary from short single-pitch cracks to long, sustained multi-pitch crack routes. Icebox Canyon holds a lot of shade, so this is a useful refuge when other Red Rock crags are too hot, though it can feel cold in winter.

nv_slab_the.blurb: An entry-level sport crag in the Calico Hills at Red Rock, sitting just left of Tuna and Chips Wall in the First Pullout zone. All 15 routes are bolted sandstone slab, running from about 5.5 to 5.10, with most in the 5.7 to 5.8 range. The walk from the pullout lot is about ten minutes and ends with a scramble down a gully, making it among the quicker approaches in the area. Good for newer leaders and anyone teaching the basics. The rock here is friable, so wearing a helmet is wise.

nv_amusement_park.blurb: A beginner-friendly sandstone wall in the First Pullout zone of the Calico Hills, Red Rock, tucked directly beneath the Panty Wall. Of its 15 routes, 12 are sport, two are top-rope and one is trad, and almost all sit around 5.7, with only a couple of easier or slightly harder lines. The wall faces north and goes into shade through the afternoon, so it stays chilly in winter but is comfortable once things warm up. Several routes share anchor stations, which makes it a good spot for teaching, though shared lines can get busy. Reach it by following the Panty Wall approach, around fifteen minutes from the road.

nv_strategic_arms_wall.blurb: A steep, black-varnished sandstone wall of roughly 100 feet high above Ash Spring in Calico Basin, Red Rock, built around a tall overhanging corner. The 14 routes are mostly bolted, with two trad lines, and all fall between 5.10 and 5.13 with the bulk at 5.11 and 5.12. This is a place for strong climbers rather than beginners. The walk in is longer than at most Calico Basin crags, around half an hour up a steepening canyon past the Cold Sweat slab, finishing with some slab scrambling and boulder-hopping. Expect a quiet day compared with the roadside walls.

nv_fish_head.blurb: A bouldering spot among the Windy Canyon Boulders on the east and south sides of Windy Peak in Red Rock, centered on a huge fish-head-shaped block that can be seen from the parking area. There are 14 problems on varnished sandstone, mostly easy to middling at V1 to V3, with a few much harder lines up to V8. Several problems carry a real consequence on the landing, so bring enough pads and spotters. The surrounding area is secluded and sees fewer people than the busier boulder fields of Red Rock. The rock is fragile, so holds can break.

nv_corrosion_cave_and_walk_by_slab.blurb: A steep limestone cave and a neighbouring slab at The Hood on Mt. Charleston, at about 7,800 feet in the Spring Mountains outside Las Vegas. All 14 routes are bolted sport climbs on smooth white limestone with pockets, ranging from 5.10 to 5.14 and concentrated between 5.11 and 5.13. This is a hard-sport destination where the cave lines are short and powerful. The altitude keeps summer temperatures much cooler than the desert floor. The trail to the base is a short but steep climb of switchbacks, around fifteen minutes in.
